title: Promotional Interest Disclosure — Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Promotional Interest Disclosure — Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

How a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan prices interest depends on the structure of its promotional term. The promotional rate, the standard rate, the penalty rate, the automatic payment reduction, the repricing trigger and the review length are the figures the rates disclosure states for the plan's term.

**Accrual during the term.** On a deferred interest term, interest accrues on the promotional balance each cycle at the term's promotional rate and is held back rather than billed; on an equal payment term the promotional rate is charged in the cycle it accrues and nothing is held back.

**Giving the held-back interest back.** Held-back interest is given back only when the balance on the plan reached zero no later than the promotional term measured in whole calendar months from the date the plan began billing. Promotional months are counted as whole calendar months from the date the plan began billing, and where the anniversary day does not exist in the closing month the boundary falls on the last day of that month. The date the plan began billing is the activation date the plan record carries.

**Billing it instead.** Where the promotional term closes with any balance outstanding on a term that forfeits, the whole of the held-back interest is billed to the plan in the cycle the term closed in, and it is billed once and not cycle by cycle.

**Automatic payment.** While automatic payment is in force the promotional rate is reduced by the term's automatic payment discount, and the reduction stops applying from the cycle in which automatic payment lapses.

**Repricing.** A plan repriced to the penalty rate after the term's missed-payment trigger keeps that rate until the term's review length of consecutive on-time payments has passed, whereupon the ordinary rate returns.

## The term boundary, on hypothetical dates

A plan on a 6-month promotional term began billing on 15 March. Whole calendar months from that date put the boundary on 15 September.

| Day the balance reached zero | Held-back interest |
|---|---|
| 14 September | Given back: the balance reached zero before the boundary |
| 15 September (the boundary day itself) | Given back: no later than the boundary is satisfied at the boundary |
| 16 September | Not given back; on a term that forfeits, the whole of the held-back interest is billed in the cycle the term closed in |

A plan that began billing on 31 January on a 6-month term reaches a closing month with no 31st, so the boundary falls on the last day of that month, 31 July being replaced by the last day where the month is shorter.
